title: Who Was Ramanujan? The Greatest Mathematician of All Time?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: A person who studies or works in mathematics.
Someone with very great and rare natural ability or skill.
The ability to understand something immediately without conscious reasoning.
A statement in mathematics that can be proved to be true.
A mathematical statement showing that two expressions are equal.
A mathematical relationship between numbers or variables.
Relating to ideas rather than physical things.

sentences.en: Today I want to talk about one of the greatest mathematicians of all time.
sentences.zh: 今天我想聊聊有史以来最伟大的数学家之一。

sentences.en: A genius who, with almost no formal training, made mathematical discoveries that still astonish experts today.
sentences.zh: 他是一位天才，在几乎没有接受过正规培训的情况下，做出了至今仍让专家们惊叹的数学发现。

sentences.en: His name is Srinivasa Ramanujan, and his story is as extraordinary as the mathematical formulas he created.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫Srinivasa Ramanujan，他的故事和创造的数学公式一样非凡。

sentences.en: Despite growing up in poverty and facing enormous challenges, Ramanujan produced ideas that continue to shape modern mathematics.
sentences.zh: 尽管在贫困中长大并面临巨大挑战，Ramanujan提出的思想至今仍在塑造现代数学。

sentences.en: This episode is part of my Greatest Scientists Series, where we explore the lives and contributions of people who transformed our understanding of the world (while learning some new English vocabulary).
sentences.zh: 这一集是我“最伟大的科学家系列”的一部分，我们将探讨那些改变了我们对世界理解的人的生活和贡献（同时学习一些新的英语词汇）。

sentences.en: And today, I want to ask an interesting question: can a mathematician like Ramanujan be considered a scientist?
sentences.zh: 今天，我想问一个有趣的问题：像Ramanujan这样的数学家能被视为科学家吗？

sentences.en: Over the next few minutes, we’ll explore his early life in India, his journey to England, the famous collaboration with G.H.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几分钟里，我们将探讨他在印度的早年生活、前往英国的旅程、与G.H.的著名合作、

sentences.en: Hardy, his remarkable discoveries, his legacy, and finally, we’ll reflect on the role of mathematics itself in the world of science.
sentences.zh: Hardy、他卓越的发现、他的遗产，最后，我们将反思数学本身在科学世界中的角色。

sentences.en: Srinivasa Ramanujan was born in 1887 in a small town in Southern India.
sentences.zh: Srinivasa Ramanujan于1887年出生于印度南部的一个小镇。

sentences.en: He came from a poor but deeply traditional family.
sentences.zh: 他出身贫寒，但家庭传统深厚。

sentences.en: His father worked as a clerk in a local shop, and his mother was a homemaker who was also very religious.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲在当地一家商店当职员，母亲是一位家庭主妇，也非常虔诚。

sentences.en: As a child, Ramanujan showed extraordinary talent for mathematics.
sentences.zh: 小的时候，Ramanujan就展现出了非凡的数学天赋。

sentences.en: While most children were learning simple addition and multiplication, Ramanujan was already exploring complex ideas entirely on his own.
sentences.zh: 当大多数孩子还在学习简单的加法和乘法时，Ramanujan就已经完全靠自己探索复杂的思想了。

sentences.en: Teachers quickly noticed that he could solve problems without using traditional methods.
sentences.zh: 老师们很快注意到他不用传统方法就能解题。

sentences.en: He could arrive at the correct answer through intuition, natural ability, rather than calculation.
sentences.zh: 他可以通过直觉和天分得出正确答案，而不是靠计算。

sentences.en: As a primary school student, Ramanujan excelled.
sentences.zh: 作为一名小学生，Ramanujan非常优秀。

sentences.en: He achieved the best exam grades in his area and at the age of 11, he already knew more mathematics than the college students who were renting rooms in his family home.
sentences.zh: 他取得了当地最好的考试成绩，在11岁时，他懂的数学知识就已经超过了在他家租房子的大学生。

sentences.en: When he was a teenager, he received a book that changed his life, “A Synopsis of Elementary Results in Pure and Applied Mathematics” by George Carr.
sentences.zh: 在他十几岁时，他得到了一本改变他一生的书——乔治·卡尔（George Carr）的《纯粹与应用数学基本结果概要》。

sentences.en: This wasn’t a typical textbook. It was basically a huge collection of thousands of mathematical results and theorems, but with very few explanations or proofs.
sentences.zh: 这不是一本典型的教科书。它基本上是数千个数学结果和定理的巨大集合，但几乎没有什么解释或证明。

sentences.en: For most people, it would have been impossible to learn from, especially for a teenager.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，要从中学习是不可能的，对一个青少年来说尤其如此。

sentences.en: But for Ramanujan, it became his teacher.
sentences.zh: 但对Ramanujan来说，这本书成了他的老师。

sentences.en: He studied every page, memorized the formulas, and began to develop his own ideas and some new equations that went beyond what the book contained.
sentences.zh: 他研究了每一页，背熟了公式，并开始发展自己的思想和一些超越书本内容的新方程。

sentences.en: However, his obsession with mathematics caused problems in school.
sentences.zh: 然而，他对数学的痴迷在学校里引起了麻烦。

sentences.en: Ramanujan ignored other subjects like English, history and science, which meant he repeatedly failed his exams.
sentences.zh: Ramanujan忽视了英语、历史和科学等其他科目，这意味着他考试屡屡不及格。

sentences.en: In 1903, for example, he had been given a scholarship to the University of Madras, but he lost the scholarship a year later after failing every class other than mathematics.
sentences.zh: 例如，在1903年，他曾获得马德拉斯大学的奖学金，但一年后因为除数学外所有课程都不及格而失去了奖学金。

sentences.en: Despite being a genius, he couldn’t complete his formal education.
sentences.zh: 尽管是个天才，他却无法完成正规教育。

sentences.en: In the years that followed, Ramanujan lived in poverty.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，Ramanujan生活在贫困之中。

sentences.en: He struggled to find work and a place to develop his mathematical skills.
sentences.zh: 他很难找到工作和发展数学技能的地方。

sentences.en: He continued to fill notebooks with pages of equations and results, but few people in India or in the world at that time understood his importance.
sentences.zh: 他继续在笔记本上填满密密麻麻的方程式和结果，但在当时的印度乃至全世界，很少有人理解他的重要性。

sentences.en: He also suffered from poor health which would remain a constant challenge throughout his life.
sentences.zh: 他还饱受健康状况不佳的困扰，这将成为他一生中挥之不去的挑战。

sentences.en: While searching for employment, Ramanujan began to interact with some of India’s top mathematicians.
sentences.zh: 在寻找工作的同时，Ramanujan开始与印度一些顶尖的数学家交流。

sentences.en: He met V. Ramaswamy Aiyer, the founder of the Indian Mathematical Society, when he was attempting to get a job in the same department that Ramaswamy worked.
sentences.zh: 当他试图在Ramaswamy工作的同一个部门找工作时，他遇到了印度数学学会创始人V. Ramaswamy Aiyer。

sentences.en: Impressed by his notebooks, Ramanujan was introduced to a variety of other prominent mathematicians.
sentences.zh: Ramaswamy对他的笔记本印象深刻，于是把Ramanujan介绍给了其他几位杰出的数学家。

sentences.en: In 1913, he made a decision that would completely change his life.
sentences.zh: 1913年，他做出一个彻底改变他一生的决定。

sentences.en: He sent a letter to G.H. Hardy, a respected mathematician at Cambridge University in England.
sentences.zh: 他给英国剑桥大学备受尊敬的数学家G.H. Hardy写了一封信。

sentences.en: The letter contained pages and pages of mathematical formulas.
sentences.zh: 信里包含了一页又一页的数学公式。

sentences.en: Many of these looked completely unfamiliar to Western mathematicians at the time.
sentences.zh: 在当时的西方数学家看来，其中许多公式都极其陌生。

sentences.en: At first, Hardy was skeptical. He thought the letter might be a joke or a mistake.
sentences.zh: 起初，Hardy持怀疑态度。他认为这封信可能是一个玩笑或是一个错误。

sentences.en: After all, it wasn’t common for a poor, self-taught person from the other side of the world to suddenly send new and original mathematical work to one of the world’s top universities.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，一个来自世界另一端的贫穷、自学成才的人，突然向世界顶尖大学之一发送全新且原创的数学作品，这并不常见。

sentences.en: But when Hardy and his colleague, J.E. Littlewood, began to study the results more carefully, they quickly realized that these were not random ideas.
sentences.zh: 但当Hardy和他的同事J.E. Littlewood开始更仔细地研究这些结果时，他们很快意识到这些绝不是随机的想法。

sentences.en: The formulas that Ramanujan had sent were deep, elegant, and most importantly, new.
sentences.zh: Ramanujan寄去的公式深邃、优雅，最重要的是，它们是崭新的。

sentences.en: Hardy later said that reading Ramanujan’s work was like “opening a treasure chest full of mathematical jewels.”
sentences.zh: Hardy后来评价说，阅读Ramanujan的作品就像是“打开了一个装满数学珍宝的宝箱。”

sentences.en: He immediately recognized that Ramanujan was a genius, perhaps one of the greatest mathematical minds in history.
sentences.zh: 他立刻认出Ramanujan是个天才，也许是历史上最伟大的数学头脑之一。

sentences.en: So he invited Ramanujan to come to Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 于是他邀请Ramanujan来到剑桥。

sentences.en: In 1914, after overcoming social and religious obstacles, including a lot of concerns from his family and his community about traveling overseas, Ramanujan made the long journey from India to the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 1914年，在克服了社会和宗教障碍，包括他的家人和社区对海外旅行的大量担忧之后，Ramanujan踏上了从印度到英国的漫长旅程。

sentences.en: It was the first time he had ever left India.
sentences.zh: 这是他第一次离开印度。

sentences.en: When Ramanujan and Hardy finally met, it was the meeting of two completely different worlds.
sentences.zh: 当Ramanujan和Hardy终于见面时，这是两个截然不同的世界的碰撞。

sentences.en: Hardy was a great mathematician who came from the Western academic system.
sentences.zh: Hardy是一位出身于西方学术体系的伟大数学家。

sentences.en: He was logical, disciplined, and focused on strict mathematical proofs, proving what you think is true.
sentences.zh: 他逻辑严密、纪律严明，专注于严格的数学证明，去证明你认为正确的东西。

sentences.en: Ramanujan, on the other hand, was intuitive and creative.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，Ramanujan则直觉敏锐、富有创造力。

sentences.en: He often wrote down results without showing any steps, without showing any of his proofs.
sentences.zh: 他经常写下结果，却不展示任何步骤，也不展示任何证明。

sentences.en: He also claimed that his inspiration came directly from his family’s goddess Namagiri, who revealed the formulas to him in dreams.
sentences.zh: 他还声称自己的灵感直接来自于他家族的女神纳玛吉里（Namagiri），女神在梦中向他显现了这些公式。

sentences.en: Their collaboration was very productive.
sentences.zh: 他们的合作非常富有成效。

sentences.en: Hardy tried to help Ramanujan formalize his discoveries and present them in a way that the mathematical world could understand.
sentences.zh: Hardy试图帮助Ramanujan将他的发现形式化，并以数学界能够理解的方式呈现出来。

sentences.en: Ramanujan, in turn, shocked Hardy with his ability to produce new and unexpected results almost effortlessly.
sentences.zh: 反过来，Ramanujan以其几乎毫不费力地产生新奇和意想不到结果的能力震惊了Hardy。

sentences.en: Hardy and Ramanujan formed one of the most remarkable partnerships in the history of science or mathematics.
sentences.zh: Hardy和Ramanujan组成了科学或数学史上最非凡的伙伴关系之一。

sentences.en: In fact, Hardy once said that his greatest contribution to mathematics was discovering Ramanujan.
sentences.zh: 事实上，Hardy曾说过，他对数学最大的贡献就是发现了Ramanujan。

sentences.en: So what did Ramanujan actually discover?
sentences.zh: 那么Ramanujan到底发现了什么？

sentences.en: This is a difficult topic to discuss. Unlike the previous scientists I’ve talked about in this series, Isaac Newton and Marie Curie.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难讨论的话题。不像我在这系列里谈论过的前几位科学家，艾萨克·牛顿和玛丽·居里。

sentences.en: Ramanujan was a mathematician working on incredibly complex things.
sentences.zh: Ramanujan是一位致力于极其复杂事物的数学家。

sentences.en: One of his most famous discoveries was the Ramanujan Prime, a special type of prime number that still appears in modern mathematical research.
sentences.zh: 他最著名的发现之一是拉马努金素数（Ramanujan Prime），这是一种至今仍出现在现代数学研究中的特殊素数。

sentences.en: A prime number is a number greater than one that can only be divided exactly by one and itself.
sentences.zh: 素数是指一个大于一的自然数，除了一和它本身外，不能被其他自然数整除。

sentences.en: For example, 3, 5, 7, 11. He also developed something known as the Ramanujan Theta function, a complex formula that later became important in fields like physics and computer science.
sentences.zh: 例如，3、5、7、11。他还开发了被称为拉马努金θ函数（Ramanujan Theta function）的东西，这是一个后来在物理学和计算机科学等领域变得非常重要的复杂公式。

sentences.en: Another contribution was his work on infinite series.
sentences.zh: 另一个贡献是他对级数的研究。

sentences.en: These are equations that add together an endless or infinite number of terms.
sentences.zh: 这些方程将无限或无数个项相加在一起。

sentences.en: Using these he found new ways to calculate the number PI with incredible accuracy.
sentences.zh: 利用这些，他找到了以惊人精度计算圆周率PI的新方法。

sentences.en: Some of his formulas are still used today in computer algorithms, which try to calculate trillions of digits of Pi.
sentences.zh: 他的某些公式至今仍用于计算机算法中，这些算法试图计算圆周率的万亿位数字。

sentences.en: Perhaps the most mysterious of his discoveries were his mock theta functions, which he discovered near the end of his life.
sentences.zh: 也许他最神秘的发现是他在生命接近尾声时发现的仿θ函数（mock theta functions）。

sentences.en: For decades, mathematicians couldn’t fully understand what these functions meant.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，数学家们无法完全理解这些函数的含义。

sentences.en: It wasn’t really until the late 20th century that they were shown to be deeply connected to modern physics, including string theory and quantum mechanics.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪后期，人们才真正发现它们与现代物理学（包括弦理论和量子力学）有着深厚的联系。

sentences.en: Ramanujan’s ideas, written in a notebook in the early 1900s, helped to explain parts of the universe that scientists would only begin to study many years later.
sentences.zh: Ramanujan在20世纪初写在笔记本上的想法，帮助解释了科学家们多年后才开始研究的部分宇宙。

sentences.en: Ramanujan’s mathematical notebooks actually contained thousands of results.
sentences.zh: Ramanujan的数学笔记本实际上包含了成千上万个结果。

sentences.en: Many of these were written without any explanation or proof.
sentences.zh: 其中许多都是在没有任何解释或证明的情况下写出来的。

sentences.en: Mathematicians have spent over a century studying and expanding upon his discoveries, and the vast majority of his results have turned out to be correct.
sentences.zh: 数学家们花了一个多世纪的时间来研究和扩展他的发现，绝大多数结果都被证明是正确的。

sentences.en: Although Ramanujan’s years in the UK were incredibly productive, they also took a serious toll on his health.
sentences.zh: 尽管Ramanujan在英国的几年多产得惊人，但这对其健康造成了严重的损害。

sentences.en: He struggled with the cold British climate, wartime food shortages, and also the difficulty of maintaining his strict vegetarian diet.
sentences.zh: 他很难适应英国寒冷的气候、战时的食物短缺，以及坚持严格素食习惯的困难。

sentences.en: He was far from home and his family, and he often felt lonely and isolated.
sentences.zh: 他远离家乡和家人，经常感到孤独和孤立。

sentences.en: On top of that, he was working constantly, pushing his body and mind to the limit.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他一直在不断工作，将自己的身体和精神推向极限。

sentences.en: By 1917, his health had begun to fail. He was diagnosed with several illnesses, including tuberculosis and vitamin deficiencies, and he spent long periods recovering in hospitals.
sentences.zh: 到1917年，他的健康状况开始恶化。他被诊断出患有多种疾病，包括结核病和维生素缺乏症，并在医院里度过了漫长的康复期。

sentences.en: He also attempted to end his own life by jumping onto train tracks in London.
sentences.zh: 他甚至曾试图跳入伦敦的火车轨道来结束自己的生命。

sentences.en: In 1919, once the First World War had ended, doctors advised him to return to India to recover in warmer climates.
sentences.zh: 1919年，第一次世界大战结束后，医生建议他返回印度，在温暖的气候中恢复健康。

sentences.en: After five years in England, Ramanujan finally went home.
sentences.zh: 在英国呆了五年后，Ramanujan终于回到了家。

sentences.en: Sadly, his health did not improve. Even in his final months, he remained dedicated to his work, writing letters to G.H.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，他的健康状况并没有改善。甚至在他生命的最后几个月里，他仍然致力于他的工作，给G.H.写信。

sentences.en: Hardy filled with new mathematical results, including those mysterious mock theta functions.
sentences.zh: Hardy信中充满了新的数学结果，包括那些神秘的仿θ函数。

sentences.en: Ramanujan died in 1920 at the age of just 32.
sentences.zh: Ramanujan于1920年去世，享年仅32岁。

sentences.en: His death was a huge loss for mathematics.
sentences.zh: 他的去世对数学界来说是一个巨大的损失。

sentences.en: Imagine what he could have discovered if he had lived another 10, 20, 30, 40 years.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果他多活10年、20年、30年、40年，他本可以发现什么。

sentences.en: But in his short life, he had produced more original ideas than most mathematicians do in an entire career.
sentences.zh: 但在他短暂的一生中，他产生的原创想法比大多数数学家在整个职业生涯中产生的还要多。

sentences.en: Even though Ramanujan died so young, his influence on mathematics was massive.
sentences.zh: 尽管Ramanujan英年早逝，但他对数学的影响是巨大的。

sentences.en: After his death, his notebooks were studied by mathematicians around the world.
sentences.zh: 在他去世后，世界各地的数学家对他的笔记本进行了研究。

sentences.en: They contained thousands of results, most of them without proofs or explanations, but almost all of them turned out to be correct.
sentences.zh: 它们包含了成千上万个结果，其中大部分没有证明或解释，但几乎所有结果都被证明是正确的。

sentences.en: In the decades that followed, his ideas became even more important.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几十年里，他的思想变得更加重要。

sentences.en: Mathematicians discovered that Ramanujan’s work could be applied to new areas, including computer science, physics, and modern theories about the universe.
sentences.zh: 数学家们发现Ramanujan的工作可以应用于新的领域，包括计算机科学、物理学以及关于宇宙的现代理论。

sentences.en: These did not even exist while Ramanujan was alive.
sentences.zh: 这些在Ramanujan活着的时候甚至还不存在。

sentences.en: In 1976, researchers found what would become known as Ramanjuan’s lost notebook, a collection of unpublished results that had been forgotten more than 50 years earlier.
sentences.zh: 1976年，研究人员发现了后来被称为Ramanujan丢失的笔记本，这是一集50多年前被遗忘的未发表结果的集合。

sentences.en: This discovery reignited interest in Ramanujan and his work and led to a new wave of research inspired by his ideas.
sentences.zh: 这一发现重新点燃了人们对Ramanujan及其工作的兴趣，并引领了受其思想启发的新一波研究浪潮。

sentences.en: Today, Ramanujan is remembered as one of the greatest mathematical minds in history.
sentences.zh: 今天，Ramanujan被铭记为历史上最伟大的数学头脑之一。

sentences.en: There’s even an academic journal called the Ramanujan Journal, dedicated to research in areas connected to his style of mathematics.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一本名为《拉马努金期刊》（Ramanujan Journal）的学术期刊，专门用于研究与他的数学风格相关的领域。

sentences.en: His story has been told in books, documentaries, and films.
sentences.zh: 他的故事已经被搬上了书籍、纪录片和电影。

sentences.en: Most famously, the “Man Who Knew Infinity” starring Dev Patel.
sentences.zh: 最著名的当属由戴夫·帕特尔（Dev Patel）主演的《知无涯者》（“Man Who Knew Infinity”）。

sentences.en: Ramanujan’s story, to me, represents the idea that great ideas can come from anywhere, not just elite universities or wealthy backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，Ramanujan的故事代表了这样一种观点：伟大的思想可以来自任何地方，而不仅仅是精英大学或富裕的背景。

sentences.en: He proved that genius can exist in the most unexpected places.​
sentences.zh: 事实证明，天才可以存在于最意想不到的地方。

sentences.en: Before we finish today’s episode, I want to think about a question.
sentences.zh: 在我们结束今天的节目之前，我想思考一个问题。

sentences.en: Is mathematics a science? And if it is, should someone like Ramanujan be remembered as one of the greatest scientists of all time?
sentences.zh: 数学是科学吗？如果是的话，像Ramanujan这样的人应该被铭记为有史以来最伟大的科学家之一吗？

sentences.en: Science is based on observation, experimentation, and evidence.
sentences.zh: 科学的基础是观察、实验和证据。

sentences.en: It’s about testing ideas against the real world.
sentences.zh: 它是关于用现实世界检验想法的。

sentences.en: Mathematics, on the other hand, is abstract.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，数学是抽象的。

sentences.en: It deals with logic, symbols, and proofs, rather than physical experiments.
sentences.zh: 它处理的是逻辑、符号和证明，而不是物理实验。

sentences.en: Mathematicians don’t look through telescopes or use microscopes.
sentences.zh: 数学家不通过望远镜或使用显微镜观察。

sentences.en: They use their minds. But if we think a little deeper, the line between science and mathematics is not clear.
sentences.zh: 他们用的是大脑。但如果我们深入思考一下，科学和数学之间的界限并不清晰。

sentences.en: Every scientific field, from physics to chemistry to computer science, depends on mathematical thinking.
sentences.zh: 每一个科学领域，从物理学、化学到计算机科学，都依赖于数学思维。

sentences.en: Mathematics gives scientists the language, the tools they need to describe, predict and understand the world, understand reality.
sentences.zh: 数学为科学家提供了描述、预测和理解世界、理解现实所需的语言和工具。

sentences.en: Without it, science as we know, could not exist.
sentences.zh: 没有它，我们所知的科学就不复存在。

sentences.en: Ramanujan might not have carried out scientific experiments, but his discoveries helped make scientific progress possible.
sentences.zh: Ramanujan可能没有进行过科学实验，但他的发现为科学进步提供了可能。

sentences.en: Maybe a scientist isn’t just someone who studies nature through experiments, but it is anyone who helps humanity uncover new truths about the world.
sentences.zh: 也许科学家不仅仅是通过实验研究自然的人，而是任何帮助人类揭开世界新真相的人。

sentences.en: Ramanujan’s story reminds us that genius can come from the most unlikely places.
sentences.zh: Ramanujan的故事提醒我们，天才可以来自最不可思议的地方。

sentences.en: He had no degree. No formal training, but his mind saw patterns in numbers that no one else could.
sentences.zh: 他没有学位，没有接受过正规训练，但他的大脑看到了别人看不到的数字规律。

sentences.en: And even a century after his death, mathematicians are still learning from him.
sentences.zh: 甚至在他去世一个世纪后，数学家们仍在向他学习。

sentences.en: What do you think? Is mathematics a science?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？数学是科学吗？

sentences.en: Should Ramanujan be remembered a alongside people like Einstein or Darwin or Newton?
sentences.zh: Ramanujan应该和爱因斯坦、达尔文或牛顿这样的人并列被世人铭记吗？
